objects.description: Function pointer type for application-provided INI parse callbacks. Called for each parsed key/value (and optionally with a line number if INI_HANDLER_LINENO is nonzero). The handler returns nonzero on success to continue parsing, or zero to signal an error for that entry.

objects.definition: typedef char* (*ini_reader)(char* str, int num, void* stream);
objects.description: Function pointer type matching fgets-like readers, used by ini_parse_stream to read lines from a custom input source. Should return str on success, or nullptr on EOF/error.

C++ helper class that parses an INI file or buffer and exposes getters for values as strings, integers, booleans, etc. Internally stores values in a map keyed by section/name and tracks an error code from parsing.

functions.name: ini_parse
functions.signature: int ini_parse(const char* filename, ini_handler handler, void* user);
functions.description: Parse an INI file from a filesystem path. For each parsed name=value pair (and optionally section starts depending on compile-time flags), the provided handler is called with user data, section, name, and value. The handler returns nonzero to accept/process the pair or zero to signal an error. Returns 0 on success, the line number of the first parse error (parsing continues), -1 if the file could not be opened, or -2 on memory allocation failure (only when heap allocation is used).
requirements: filename must point to a valid, readable file path string (NUL-terminated).
handler must be a valid function pointer of type ini_handler.
user may be any pointer and is passed through to handler unchanged.
Within ini_handler: the section and name strings must not be modified; the value string may be cast to char* and modified, and is valid only for the duration of the handler call.
ini_handler must return nonzero on success for each call; returning zero indicates an error for that line.
Caller must interpret nonzero return values and negative error codes as documented.

functions.name: ini_parse_file
functions.signature: int ini_parse_file(FILE* file, ini_handler handler, void* user);
functions.description: Parse an INI file from an already-open FILE*. Behavior matches ini_parse() regarding syntax and handler invocation. Does not close the FILE*; the caller retains ownership and must close it. Returns 0 on success, line number of first parse error, or -2 on memory allocation failure (only when heap allocation is used).
requirements: file must be a valid, open FILE* positioned where parsing should begin.
This function does not close file; the caller must close it when done.
handler must be a valid function pointer of type ini_handler; user is passed through.
Within ini_handler: section and name must not be modified; value is valid only during the call and may be cast to char* and modified.
ini_handler must return nonzero on success; zero indicates an error for that line.

functions.name: ini_parse_stream
functions.signature: int ini_parse_stream(ini_reader reader, void* stream, ini_handler handler, void* user);
functions.description: Parse INI data using a custom fgets-style reader function and a stream/context pointer. Useful for custom I/O sources (e.g., memory buffers, sockets). For each parsed name=value pair, calls the handler with user data, section, name, and value. Returns 0 on success, line number of first parse error, or -2 on memory allocation failure (only when heap allocation is used).
requirements: reader must be a valid function pointer of type ini_reader: char* (*)(char* str, int num, void* stream), and must behave like fgets(), filling str with up to num-1 characters and NUL-terminating on success or returning NULL on EOF/error.
stream is passed to reader on each call; its type/ownership are user-defined.
handler must be a valid ini_handler; user is passed through to handler.
Within ini_handler: section and name must not be modified; value is valid only during the call and may be cast to char* and modified.
ini_handler must return nonzero on success; zero indicates an error for that line.

functions.name: ini_parse_string
functions.signature: int ini_parse_string(const char* string, ini_handler handler, void* user);
functions.description: Parse INI data from a NUL-terminated string in memory. Equivalent to ini_parse() but sources input from the provided string. Calls handler for each parsed pair. Returns 0 on success, line number of first parse error, or -2 on memory allocation failure (only when heap allocation is used).
requirements: string must point to a valid NUL-terminated buffer containing INI data.
handler must be a valid ini_handler; user is passed through.
Within ini_handler: section and name must not be modified; value is valid only during the call and may be cast to char* and modified.
ini_handler must return nonzero on success; zero indicates an error for that line.

functions.name: ini_parse_string_length
functions.signature: int ini_parse_string_length(const char* string, size_t length, ini_handler handler, void* user);
functions.description: Parse INI data from a memory buffer with explicit length, avoiding strlen(). Useful for buffers that may contain NULs or are not NUL-terminated. Calls handler for each parsed pair. Returns 0 on success, line number of first parse error, or -2 on memory allocation failure (only when heap allocation is used).
requirements: string must point to a buffer of at least length bytes containing INI-formatted data.
length specifies the number of bytes to parse; data need not be NUL-terminated.
handler must be a valid ini_handler; user is passed through.
Within ini_handler: section and name must not be modified; value is valid only during the call and may be cast to char* and modified.
ini_handler must return nonzero on success; zero indicates an error for that line.

functions.name: INIReader::INIReader
functions.signature: explicit INIReader::INIReader(const std::string& filename);
functions.description: Construct an INIReader and parse the specified file. Parsing semantics are those of inih (see ini.h). Parsing status can be retrieved via ParseError() and ParseErrorMessage().
requirements: filename must reference a readable file path string.
Construction will perform parsing immediately; callers should check ParseError() to determine success.

functions.name: INIReader::ParseError
functions.signature: int INIReader::ParseError() const;
functions.description: Return the result code from parsing: 0 on success, line number of first parse error, -1 on file open error (when constructed from filename), or -2 on memory allocation error.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed INIReader instance.

functions.name: INIReader::ParseErrorMessage
functions.signature: std::string INIReader::ParseErrorMessage() const;
functions.description: Return a human-readable message describing the parsing error that occurred, or an empty string if there was no error.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed INIReader instance.

functions.name: INIReader::Get
functions.signature: std::string INIReader::Get(const std::string& section, const std::string& name, const std::string& default_value) const;
functions.description: Retrieve a raw string value for the given section and name. Returns default_value if the key is not present.
requirements: section is matched as provided; it should refer to a section name as parsed.
name is the key within the section.
default_value is returned when the key is missing.

requirements: section and name select the desired key.
default_value is returned when the key is missing or the value is empty/whitespace.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid INI-formatted content bytes suitable for
# filenames consumed by the target fuzz stubs. It aims to cover diverse features
# of INI syntax to exercise different code paths: sections, key/value pairs,
# comments, whitespace variations, booleans, numbers (dec/hex), floats, empty
# values, quoted values, escapes, duplicates, multi-section keys, and long lines.

TRUE_TOKENS = ["true", "yes", "on", "1", "TRUE", "Yes", "On"]
FALSE_TOKENS = ["false", "no", "off", "0", "FALSE", "No", "Off"]

SECTION_NAMES = [
    "default",
    "network",
    "database",
    "paths",
    "unicode",
    "a.b.c",          # dotted
    "with spaces",     # spaces
    "Mixed-Case",
    "empty",
]

KEY_NAMES = [
    "key",
    "answer",
    "enabled",
    "threshold",
    "pi",
    "hexval",
    "path",
    "empty",
    "list",
    "user_name",
    "timeout_ms",
    "rate.hz",
]

# Some value pools to cover getters in INIReader
STRING_VALUES = [
    "hello",
    "world",
    "spaced value",
    "quoted value",
    "tab\tseparated",
    "utf8-✓",
    "with#hash",
    "with;semi",
    "brackets[]",
    ""
]

PATH_VALUES = [
    "/usr/local/bin",
    "C:\\Program Files\\App",
    "./relative/path",
    "..\\parent\\dir",
]

DEC_INTS = ["0", "1", "-1", "42", "-999999", "2147483647", "-2147483648", "9223372036854775807", "-9223372036854775808"]
HEX_INTS = ["0x0", "0x1", "0X2A", "0x7fffffff", "0x80000000", "0xffffffffffffffff"]
FLOATS = ["0.0", "3.14159", "-2.5", "1e3", "-1E-6", ".5", "inf", "-inf", "nan"]

# Build a long but valid line to probe buffer handling while staying under 4096 bytes

def long_value(length: int) -> str:
    core = "A" * max(0, length)
    return core


def rnd(r: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[r.randrange(len(arr))]


def maybe_ws(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Random leading/trailing whitespace
    spaces = " " * r.randrange(0, 3)
    tabs = "\t" * r.randrange(0, 2)
    return spaces + tabs


def emit_comment(r: random.Random) -> str:
    starter = rnd(r, [';', '#'])
    body_choices = [
        " just a comment",
        " section note",
        " key=value in comment",
        " unicode ✓",
        "",
    ]
    return f"{starter}{rnd(r, body_choices)}\n"


def emit_section(r: random.Random, name: str = None) -> str:
    if name is None:
        name = rnd(r, SECTION_NAMES)
    # Optionally add whitespace around name
    pre = maybe_ws(r)
    post = maybe_ws(r)
    return f"[{pre}{name}{post}]\n"


def emit_keyval(r: random.Random, key: str = None, value: str = None) -> str:
    if key is None:
        key = rnd(r, KEY_NAMES)
    # value selection designed to cover numeric, boolean, strings, quoted, empty
    if value is None:
        pick = r.randrange(0, 10)
        if pick == 0:
            value = rnd(r, TRUE_TOKENS)
        elif pick == 1:
            value = rnd(r, FALSE_TOKENS)
        elif pick == 2:
            value = rnd(r, DEC_INTS)
        elif pick == 3:
            value = rnd(r, HEX_INTS)
        elif pick == 4:
            value = rnd(r, FLOATS)
        elif pick == 5:
            value = rnd(r, PATH_VALUES)
        elif pick == 6:
            value = rnd(r, STRING_VALUES)
        elif pick == 7:
            # quoted value possibly with escapes
            body = rnd(r, STRING_VALUES).replace('"', '\\"')
            value = f'"{body}"'
        elif pick == 8:
            # empty value
            value = ""
        else:
            # long value but limited length
            value = long_value(r.randrange(32, 256))
    # Choose separator style and whitespace
    sep = rnd(r, ['=', ':'])
    pre_ws = maybe_ws(r)
    post_ws = maybe_ws(r)
    # Optionally append inline comment after value
    tail = ""
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        tail = maybe_ws(r) + rnd(r, ['; note', '# trailing comment'])
    return f"{key}{pre_ws}{sep}{post_ws}{value}{tail}\n"


def emit_blank(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Possibly whitespace-only line
    return (" " * r.randrange(0, 3) + "\t" * r.randrange(0, 2)) + "\n"


def build_ini(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # File header comments and BOM-like start (without actual BOM bytes to keep it ASCII/UTF-8)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(emit_comment(r))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append(emit_blank(r))

    # Optionally some global (no section) keys
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 5)):
            lines.append(emit_keyval(r))

    # Emit several sections with varied content
    num_sections = r.randrange(2, 6)
    used_sections = r.sample(SECTION_NAMES, k=min(num_sections, len(SECTION_NAMES)))
    for s in used_sections:
        lines.append(emit_section(r, s))
        # Mix of blank lines and comments
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(emit_comment(r))
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            lines.append(emit_blank(r))
        # Emit some keys
        nkeys = r.randrange(2, 8)
        for _ in range(nkeys):
            lines.append(emit_keyval(r))
        # Optional duplicate keys to test overwrite behavior
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            dup_key = rnd(r, KEY_NAMES)
            lines.append(emit_keyval(r, dup_key, rnd(r, STRING_VALUES)))
            lines.append(emit_keyval(r, dup_key, rnd(r, DEC_INTS + HEX_INTS)))

    # Trailing whitespace/comments
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append(emit_comment(r))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(emit_blank(r))

    text = "".join(lines)

    # Ensure size constraints (<= 4096 bytes). If too long, truncate at a newline boundary.
    b = text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > target_size:
        # Try to cut at last newline before limit for integrity
        cut = b.rfind(b"\n", 0, target_size)
        if cut == -1:
            cut = target_size
        b = b[:cut]
        text = b.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Ensure final newline to complete last line
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Aim for a broad range of sizes while staying under 4 KiB
    target_size = r.randrange(256, 2048)
    ini_text = build_ini(r, target_size)

    # Occasionally craft a tiny focused INI to target specific getters
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        focused = []
        focused.append("; focused values for getters\n")
        focused.append("[numbers]\n")
        focused.append("int_dec = 12345\n")
        focused.append("int_hex = 0x2A\n")
        focused.append("u64 = 0xffffffffffffffff\n")
        focused.append("real = -3.5e2\n")
        focused.append("[bools]\n")
        focused.append("t1 = true\n")
        focused.append("t2 = On\n")
        focused.append("f1 = false\n")
        focused.append("f2 = 0\n")
        focused.append("[strings]\n")
        focused.append('quoted = "a quoted string"\n')
        focused.append("empty = \n")
        focused.append("path = /usr/bin\n")
        ini_text = "".join(focused)

    data = ini_text.encode("utf-8")
    # Final safety cap at 4096 bytes
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
        # Try to end at newline for cleanliness
        nl = data.rfind(b"\n")
        if nl != -1:
            data = data[:nl+1]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generate valid INI text with sections, keys, values, comments and varied value types.
# The buffer should be NUL-terminated when consumed as C-string; Python bytes will include a trailing \0.

TRUE_TOKENS = ["true", "yes", "on", "1"]
FALSE_TOKENS = ["false", "no", "off", "0"]
NUM_SAMPLES = [
    "0", "1", "-1", "42", "-273", "2147483647", "-2147483648",
    "0x0", "0x1", "0x7fffffff", "0XFFFFFFFF", "0xDEADBEEF", "0x80000000"
]
REAL_SAMPLES = [
    "0.0", "-0.0", "3.14159", "-1.5e-10", "6.022e23", ".5", "1.", "-2."
]
WHITES = [" ", "\t"]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_" )
    rest_len = rng.randint(min_len-1, max_len-1)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    return first + "".join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(rest_len))

def _maybe_ws(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return "".join(rng.choice(WHITES) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
    return ""

def _quoted(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Optionally quote and include escaped characters
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # Basic escaping for quotes and backslashes
        esc = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
        return f'"{esc}"'
    return s

def _comment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Comments using ';' or '#', possibly after whitespace
    leader = rng.choice([';', '#'])
    text = rng.choice([
        " a comment", " note", "", " trailing" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""])
    return f"{leader}{text}"

def _kv_pair(rng: random.Random, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    # Add optional whitespace around '=' and after key, support inline comments
    ws1 = _maybe_ws(rng)
    ws2 = _maybe_ws(rng)
    line = f"{key}{ws1}={ws2}{value}"
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        line += _maybe_ws(rng) + _comment(rng)
    return line

def _values_for_variety(rng: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    # Provide diverse keys -> values to exercise getters
    vals: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    # Strings, including empty and whitespace-only
    vals.append(("greeting", _quoted(rng, "hello")))
    vals.append(("empty", ""))
    vals.append(("spaces", "   "))
    # Boolean true/false with varied case
    vals.append(("flag_true", rng.choice(TRUE_TOKENS).upper() if rng.random()<0.5 else rng.choice(TRUE_TOKENS)))
    vals.append(("flag_false", rng.choice(FALSE_TOKENS).title() if rng.random()<0.5 else rng.choice(FALSE_TOKENS)))
    # Integers (dec and hex)
    vals.append(("int_dec", rng.choice(NUM_SAMPLES)))
    vals.append(("int_hex", rng.choice([v for v in NUM_SAMPLES if v.lower().startswith("0x")])))
    # Unsigned edge-ish
    vals.append(("u64", rng.choice(["0", "18446744073709551615", "0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"])) )
    # 64-bit signed
    vals.append(("i64", rng.choice(["-9223372036854775808", "9223372036854775807", "0x7fffffffffffffff"])) )
    # Reals
    vals.append(("real", rng.choice(REAL_SAMPLES)))
    # Mixed tokens with inline spaces and tabs
    vals.append(("path", _quoted(rng, "/usr/local/bin")))
    vals.append(("name", _quoted(rng, "Alice Bob")))
    # Value containing '=' and ';' inside quotes
    vals.append(("tricky", _quoted(rng, "a=b;not_comment")))
    # Value with escaped characters
    vals.append(("escape", _quoted(rng, "line1\\nline2\\tend")))
    return vals

def _section_block(rng: random.Random, name: str) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Optional leading comment and blank lines
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append(_comment(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append("")
    ws_before = _maybe_ws(rng)
    ws_after = _maybe_ws(rng)
    lines.append(f"{ws_before}[{name}]{ws_after}")

    # Some kv pairs
    for k, v in _values_for_variety(rng):
        key = k
        # Sometimes duplicate key to test last-wins behavior
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            key = k
        # Add optional whitespace in key name
        line = _kv_pair(rng, key, v)
        lines.append(line)
        # Occasionally a duplicate of same key with different value
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            alt_v = v
            # change value type a bit
            choices = TRUE_TOKENS + FALSE_TOKENS + NUM_SAMPLES + REAL_SAMPLES + ["text", _quoted(rng, ""), _quoted(rng, "dup")]
            alt_v = rng.choice(choices)
            lines.append(_kv_pair(rng, key, alt_v))
        # Add blank or comment lines between
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            lines.append("")
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            lines.append(_comment(rng))
    return lines

def _global_block(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Global (no-section) keys are allowed in many INI parsers
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(_kv_pair(rng, "global_key", _quoted(rng, "global")))
        lines.append(_kv_pair(rng, "enabled", rng.choice(TRUE_TOKENS + FALSE_TOKENS)))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            lines.append(_comment(rng))
    return lines

def _build_ini(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Optional BOM to exercise readers that might see it; inih typically ignores UTF-8 BOM
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("\ufeff")

    # Header comments
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        lines.append(_comment(rng))

    lines += _global_block(rng)

    # Generate several sections with varied names
    section_count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    used = set()
    for _ in range(section_count):
        name = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10)
        # Ensure uniqueness
        while name in used:
            name = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10)
        used.add(name)
        lines += _section_block(rng, name)

    # Trailing whitespace, blank lines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        lines.append("")

    # Join with newlines. Ensure the last line ends with a newline so fgets-like reader gets final record.
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a mix of multiple INI documents concatenated, to test parsing where only the first is relevant
    # or to feed ini_parse_stream with ample data spanning many lines.
    parts: List[str] = []
    doc_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(doc_count):
        parts.append(_build_ini(rng))
        # Sometimes insert extra blank lines between docs
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append("\n")

    ini_text = "".join(parts)

    # Ensure size limit; if too large, trim at a line boundary
    max_bytes = 4096 - 1  # leave space for trailing NUL
    b = ini_text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > max_bytes:
        # Trim to last newline within limit to keep lines whole
        cut = b.rfind(b"\n", 0, max_bytes)
        if cut <= 0:
            cut = max_bytes
        b = b[:cut]
        if not b.endswith(b"\n"):
            b += b"\n"

    # Return with an explicit NUL terminator to satisfy c_str use cases
    return b + b"\x00"

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# INI generator for ini_parse_string_length fuzz target
# Generates valid INI content (may include NULs), with varied sections/keys/values
# Size limited to <= 4096 bytes

TRUE_TOKENS = ["true", "True", "TRUE", "yes", "on", "1"]
FALSE_TOKENS = ["false", "False", "FALSE", "no", "off", "0"]

DEC_SAMPLES = ["0", "1", "-1", "42", "-2147483648", "2147483647", "9223372036854775807", "-9223372036854775808"]
HEX_SAMPLES = ["0x0", "0x1", "0XDEADBEEF", "0x7fffffff", "0x80000000", "0xffffffffffffffff"]
REAL_SAMPLES = ["0.0", "-0.0", "3.14159", "-2.5", "1e10", "-1E-10", "inf", "-inf", "nan"]

# Some unicode-ish names and values (INI is usually bytes/ASCII, but many parsers accept UTF-8)
UNICODE_NAMES = ["ключ", "名前", "τ", "секция", "π", "ключ2"]

SAFE_NAME_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-./"  # avoid '=' and brackets in names
SAFE_VALUE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+,;@()[]{}<>|^%$#~"  # avoid leading ';' when needed


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, allow_unicode: bool = True, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    if allow_unicode and rng.random() < 0.25:
        return _rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_NAMES)
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Ensure not empty and no trailing spaces
    return s.strip() or "x"


def _rand_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    kind = rng.random()
    if kind < 0.15:
        return _rand_choice(rng, TRUE_TOKENS)
    if kind < 0.30:
        return _rand_choice(rng, FALSE_TOKENS)
    if kind < 0.45:
        return _rand_choice(rng, DEC_SAMPLES)
    if kind < 0.55:
        return _rand_choice(rng, HEX_SAMPLES)
    if kind < 0.70:
        return _rand_choice(rng, REAL_SAMPLES)
    # generic string
    n = rng.randint(0, 40)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_VALUE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Occasionally include quotes
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = '"' + s + '"'
    return s


def _comment_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # inih supports ';' and '#' comments (typical). Mix with whitespace.
    prefix = ';' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '#'
    ws_left = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3)
    ws_right = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3)
    body_len = rng.randint(0, 30)
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_VALUE_CHARS) for _ in range(body_len))
    return f"{ws_left}{prefix}{ws_right}{body}"


def _section_line(name: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Optionally include whitespace around name
    left_ws = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 1)
    right_ws = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 1)
    return f"[{left_ws}{name}{right_ws}]"


def _kv_line(key: str, value: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Optionally include spaces around '=' and inline comments
    lws = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2)
    rws = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2)
    line = f"{key}{lws}={rws}{value}"
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # add inline comment using ';' or '#'
        sep = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3)
        c = ';' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '#'
        line += f"{sep}{c}{sep}note"
    return line


def _generate_ini(rng: random.Random, target_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    lines: List[bytes] = []

    # Optionally start with BOM or UTF-8 BOM-like bytes to exercise handling
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append(b"\xef\xbb\xbf")

    # Top-level comments and blank lines before any section
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            lines.append((_comment_line(rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            lines.append(b"\n")

    num_sections = rng.randint(1, 6)

    # Some keys before any section (global section)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        num_globals = rng.randint(1, 5)
        for _ in range(num_globals):
            key = _rand_ident(rng)
            val = _rand_value(rng)
            lines.append((_kv_line(key, val, rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))
        lines.append(b"\n")

    for sidx in range(num_sections):
        sname = _rand_ident(rng)
        lines.append((_section_line(sname, rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))

        # Optional comments/blank lines after section header
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                lines.append((_comment_line(rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))
            else:
                lines.append(b"\n")

        # A mix of booleans, integers, hex, real, and strings
        nkeys = rng.randint(2, 12)
        used_keys = set()
        for _ in range(nkeys):
            key = _rand_ident(rng)
            # Ensure unique keys to exercise map behavior
            if key in used_keys:
                key += str(rng.randint(0, 9))
            used_keys.add(key)
            val = _rand_value(rng)
            lines.append((_kv_line(key, val, rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))

        # Occasionally add duplicate keys with different values to test overwrite
        if rng.random() < 0.4 and used_keys:
            dup_key = _rand_choice(rng, list(used_keys))
            val = _rand_value(rng)
            lines.append((_kv_line(dup_key, val, rng) + "\n").encode('utf-8'))

        # Blank line between sections
        lines.append(b"\n")

    blob = b"".join(lines)

    # Optionally insert NUL bytes in safe places to exercise length-bound parsing.
    # We keep them between lines so that typical parsers still handle segments up to NUL if they ignore it,
    # but ini_parse_string_length will rely on explicit length and still see following bytes.
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(blob) > 0:
        insertions = rng.randint(1, min(5, max(1, len(blob) // 50)))
        for _ in range(insertions):
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(blob))
            blob = blob[:pos] + b"\x00" + blob[pos:]

    # Trim to target size while ensuring not to cut in the middle of multi-byte UTF-8 sequences unfairly.
    # As we're using UTF-8 and ASCII, naive truncation is acceptable for fuzzing; parser uses bytes with explicit length.
    return blob[:target_bytes]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target size within reasonable bounds, leaving headroom for fuzzer to vary len
    base_size = rng.randint(64, 1200)
    # Ensure upper bound
    target_bytes = min(4096, base_size)
    data = _generate_ini(rng, target_bytes)
    # Guarantee non-empty output to let the fuzzer pick length 0..N
    if not data:
        data = b"key=value\n"
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# We generate a valid INI buffer intended to be consumed by INIReader(buffer, size)
# and by ini_parse_string(_length). The fuzz stubs then query sections/keys and
# parse values as string/integer/unsigned/integer64/real/boolean.
# Our goal: create diverse, valid INI with multiple sections, duplicate keys,
# comments, continuations, whitespace-only values, empty values, quoted values,
# different numeral bases, large/small floats, booleans with varied casings,
# and keys with characters that are commonly edge-y but still valid for INI.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
WS = [" ", "\t"]
BOOL_TRUE = ["true", "TRUE", "Yes", "on", "1", "yEs"]
BOOL_FALSE = ["false", "FALSE", "No", "off", "0", "nO"]


def r(seed: int) -> random.Random:
    return random.Random(seed)


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    # Alphanumeric string as per known data type; allow some punctuation commonly seen in INI keys
    extra = "_-.:/"
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = ALNUM + extra
    s = rng.choice(ALNUM)  # start with alnum to keep it friendly
    for _ in range(length - 1):
        s += rng.choice(chars)
    return s


def rand_section_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include some nesting and dots to simulate real-world INI
    parts = [rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    return ".".join(parts)


def rand_comment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    leader = rng.choice([';', '#'])
    text = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + ' _-.:/\t') for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 40)))
    return f"{leader}{text}"


def rand_ws(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(WS) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))


def value_integer(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # decimal
        n = rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
        return str(n)
    else:
        # hex with optional sign
        n = rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1)
        s = f"0x{n:x}"
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            s = s.replace('x', 'X')
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            s = ("-" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "+") + s
        return s


def value_unsigned(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1))
    else:
        n = rng.randint(0, 2**64 - 1)
        s = f"0x{n:x}"
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = s.replace('x', 'X')
        return s


def value_real(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.35:
        # simple float
        return f"{rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6):.6f}"
    elif choice < 0.7:
        # scientific
        mant = rng.uniform(-9.9, 9.9)
        exp = rng.randint(-308, 308)
        return f"{mant}e{exp}"
    else:
        # integers as valid reals
        return str(rng.randint(-10**12, 10**12))


def value_boolean(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(BOOL_TRUE + BOOL_FALSE)


def value_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # include spaces, punctuation, and possibly quoted strings
    modes = ['plain', 'quoted', 'spaces', 'empty', 'whitespace']
    m = rng.choice(modes)
    if m == 'plain':
        length = rng.randint(1, 24)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + '._-/:,') for _ in range(length))
    if m == 'quoted':
        # double-quoted; INI parsers often keep quotes, but still valid content
        length = rng.randint(0, 20)
        inner = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + ' _-/:,.') for _ in range(length))
        return f'"{inner}"'
    if m == 'spaces':
        left = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3)
        right = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3)
        core = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + '._-/:,') for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)))
        return left + core + right
    if m == 'empty':
        return ''
    # whitespace-only
    return ' ' * rng.randint(1, 6)


def kv_line(rng: random.Random, key: str, value: str, sep: str = '=') -> str:
    # Produce a key=value with optional whitespace and possible inline comment
    pre_ws = rand_ws(rng)
    mid_ws_l = rand_ws(rng)
    mid_ws_r = rand_ws(rng)
    post_ws = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        post_ws = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3) + rng.choice([';',' #'][0:1])  # prefer ';' inline
        # inline comment text
        post_ws += ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + ' _-') for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10)))
    return f"{pre_ws}{key}{mid_ws_l}{sep}{mid_ws_r}{value}{post_ws}"


def continued_value(rng: random.Random, base_value: str) -> List[str]:
    # Create a multi-line value using line continuation (ending with '\\')
    lines = []
    parts = [base_value]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        length = rng.randint(1, 16)
        parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + ' _-/:,.') for _ in range(length)))
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        if i < len(parts) - 1:
            lines.append(p + ' \\\n')
        else:
            lines.append(p)
    return lines


def build_section(rng: random.Random, name: str) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Section header
    lines.append(f"[{name}]")

    # Emit a mix of keys
    keys = set()

    def unique_key() -> str:
        for _ in range(10):
            k = rand_ident(rng, 1, 14)
            if k not in keys:
                keys.add(k)
                return k
        k = k if 'k' in locals() else rand_ident(rng, 1, 14)
        keys.add(k)
        return k

    # 1) Strings for Get/GetString
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        k = unique_key()
        v = value_string(rng)
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # 2) Integers (signed/hex)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        k = unique_key()
        v = value_integer(rng)
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # 3) Unsigned
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        k = unique_key()
        v = value_unsigned(rng)
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # 4) Reals
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        k = unique_key()
        v = value_real(rng)
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # 5) Booleans
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        k = unique_key()
        v = value_boolean(rng)
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # 6) Empty and whitespace-only values for GetString defaulting behavior
    k_empty = unique_key()
    lines.append(kv_line(rng, k_empty, ''))
    k_ws = unique_key()
    lines.append(kv_line(rng, k_ws, ' ' * rng.randint(1, 5)))

    # 7) Duplicate key with different value to exercise overwrite behavior
    if keys:
        dup_key = rng.choice(list(keys))
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, dup_key, value_string(rng)))

    # 8) Continued value
    k_cont = unique_key()
    cont_parts = continued_value(rng, value_string(rng) or 'part')
    # First line with key=
    if cont_parts:
        first = cont_parts[0]
        rest = cont_parts[1:]
        lines.append(kv_line(rng, k_cont, first))
        lines.extend(rest)

    return lines


def assemble_ini(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Top-level comments and blank lines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            lines.append(rand_comment(rng))
        else:
            lines.append("")

    # Global (no section) keys: allowed by many parsers; included to broaden coverage
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
            k = rand_ident(rng, 1, 12)
            v = value_string(rng)
            lines.append(kv_line(rng, k, v))

    # Create multiple sections
    n_sections = rng.randint(2, 5)
    sec_names = []
    for _ in range(n_sections):
        name = rand_section_name(rng)
        # ensure uniqueness
        while name in sec_names:
            name = rand_section_name(rng)
        sec_names.append(name)
        lines.extend(build_section(rng, name))
        # Insert interspersed comments/blank lines
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
            lines.append(rand_comment(rng) if rng.random() < 0.7 else "")

    # Trailing whitespace and comment
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        lines.append(rand_comment(rng))

    # Join
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    # Ensure within size
    if len(text.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_BYTES:
        # Truncate on line boundary to keep validity
        out_lines = []
        total = 0
        for ln in lines:
            enc = (ln + "\n").encode('utf-8')
            if total + len(enc) > MAX_BYTES:
                break
            out_lines.append(ln)
            total += len(enc)
        text = "\n".join(out_lines)
        if not text.endswith("\n"):
            text += "\n"
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = r(seed)
    ini_text = assemble_ini(rng)
    return ini_text.encode('utf-8')
